facts.text: Residencies have been a staple of the Strip since 1944, when Liberace began a long‑term engagement at the Hotel Last Frontier, followed by legends like Louis Armstrong, Nat King Cole, Elvis Presley, and Frank Sinatra.
The Strip got its name from Los Angeles police officer Guy McAfee, who called it after his hometown’s Sunset Strip in Hollywood.
Next to MGM Grand, the Showcase Mall features a 100‑foot Coca‑Cola bottle that towers over the Strip’s skyline.
In 2021 the Pinball Hall of Fame relocated near the “Fabulous Las Vegas” sign at the south end of the Strip, bringing arcade nostalgia to the heart of the city.
A 2024 proposal unveiled an NBA‑ready arena on the Strip as part of the planned LVXP resort development, aiming to add a major sports venue to the corridor.
A new stadium and hotel are slated to open in 2028 for the MLB season, marking the Strip’s first major sports complex in decades.
